definition: A model whose trained parameters (weights) are publicly released, allowing others to download, run, and often fine-tune it themselves.
details: Open-weight models (such as LLaMA and Mistral variants) contrast with closed, API-only models, and enable broader research access, customization, and local/private deployment, while raising distinct safety and misuse considerations.

explainer.lead: An open-weight model is one whose trained parameters are publicly released so others can download, run, and often fine-tune it. It matters because it broadens research access, customization, and local or private deployment.

tiers.eli5: It's a trained AI whose finished settings are handed out, so you can run it on your own machine.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers download open-weight models such as LLaMA and Mistral variants to fine-tune them or deploy locally for privacy. Pitfall: releasing weights raises distinct safety and misuse considerations that closed, API-only models do not.
tiers.paperLevel: A model whose trained parameters (weights) are publicly released, allowing download, execution, and often fine-tuning; contrasts with closed, API-only models.

explainer.example: A team downloads a LLaMA variant and fine-tunes it on their own data for a private deployment.
